arxiv-1808-08015.title: An Enhanced SCMA Detector Enabled by Deep Neural Network
arxiv-1808-08015.creator: Chao Lu, Wei Xu, Hong Shen, Hua Zhang, and Xiaohu You
arxiv-1808-08015.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a learning approach for sparse code multiple access (SCMA) signal detection by using a deep neural network via unfolding the procedure of message passing algorithm (MPA). The MPA can be converted to a sparsely connected neural network if we treat the weights as the parameters of a neural network.

arxiv-2004-14886.title: Unitary Functor Calculus with Reality Thanks: The author wishes to thank David Barnes for numerous helpful and insightful conversations and suggestions on this material.
arxiv-2004-14886.creator: Niall Taggart
arxiv-2004-14886.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Niall Taggart. We construct a calculus of functors in the spirit of orthogonal calculus, which is designed to study “functors with reality” such as the Real classifying space functor, BU ℝ ⁡ ( − ) \BU_{\mathbb{R}}(-) . The calculus produces a Taylor tower, the n n –th layer of which is classified by a spectrum with an action of C 2 ⋉ U ⁡ ( n ) C_{2}\ltimes\mathrm{U}(n) .

arxiv-2206-07653.title: A Valid Quantization of a Half-Harmonic Oscillator Field Theory
arxiv-2206-07653.creator: John R. Klauder
arxiv-2206-07653.description: Abstract The usual full- and half-harmonic oscillators are turned into field theories, and that behavior is examined using canonical and affine quantization. The result leads to a valid affine quantization of the half harmonic oscillator field theory, which points toward further valid quantizations of more realistic field theory models.

arxiv-2207-13190.title: Chapter 58: How does artificial intelligence contribute to iEEG research?
arxiv-2207-13190.creator: Julia Berezutskaya, Anne-Lise Saive, Karim Jerbi & Marcel van Gerven
arxiv-2207-13190.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is a fast-growing field focused on modeling and machine implementation of various cognitive functions with an increasing number of applications in computer vision, text processing, robotics, neurotechnology, bio-inspired computing and others. In this chapter, we describe how AI methods can be applied in the context of intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) research.

arxiv-2304-05832.title: Few Shot Semantic Segmentation: a review of methodologies, benchmarks, and open challenges DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Journal: JACM Volume: 37 4 111 8 CCS: Computing methodologies Image segmentation CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning
arxiv-2304-05832.creator: Nico Catalano, Matteo Matteucci
arxiv-2304-05832.description: Abstract . Semantic segmentation, vital for applications ranging from autonomous driving to robotics, faces significant challenges in domains where collecting large annotated datasets is difficult or prohibitively expensive. In such contexts, such as medicine and agriculture, the scarcity of training images hampers progress.

arxiv-2406-15955.title: Beyond the Doors of Perception: Vision Transformers Represent Relations Between Objects
arxiv-2406-15955.creator: Michael A. Lepori, Alexa R. Tartaglini, Wai Keen Vong, Thomas Serre, Brenden M. Lake, Ellie Pavlick
arxiv-2406-15955.description: Abstract Though vision transformers (ViTs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance in a variety of settings, they exhibit surprising failures when performing tasks involving visual relations. This begs the question: how do ViTs attempt to perform tasks that require computing visual relations between objects? Prior efforts to interpret ViTs tend to focus on characterizing relevant low-level visual features .

arxiv-2410-04817.title: Resource-Efficient Multiview Perception: Integrating Semantic Masking with Masked Autoencoders
arxiv-2410-04817.creator: Kosta Dakic †, Kanchana Thilakarathna †, Rodrigo N. Calheiros ⋆, Teng Joon Lim †
arxiv-2410-04817.description: Abstract Multiview systems have become a key technology in modern computer vision, offering advanced capabilities in scene understanding and analysis. However, these systems face critical challenges in bandwidth limitations and computational constraints, particularly for resource-limited camera nodes like drones. This paper presents a novel approach for communication-efficient distributed multiview detection and tracking using masked autoencoders (MAEs).

arxiv-2502-02374.description: Abstract The RPCs employed at the LHC experiments are currently operated in avalanche mode, with a mixture containing a large fraction of C 2 H 2 F 4 ( ≈ \approx 90% or more) with the addition of i-C 4 H 10 and SF 6 in different concentrations.

arxiv-2502-05160.title: A parameter study for LLL and BKZ with application to shortest vector problems
arxiv-2502-05160.creator: Tobias Köppl 1 , René Zander 2 , Louis Henkel 3 , Nikolay Tcholtchev 4
arxiv-2502-05160.description: Abstract In this work, we study the solution of shortest vector problems (SVPs) arising in terms of learning with error problems (LWEs). LWEs are linear systems of equations over a modular ring, where a perturbation vector is added to the right-hand side.

arxiv-2503-24289.title: Rec-R1: Bridging Generative Large Language Models and User-Centric Recommendation Systems via Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2503-24289.creator: Jiacheng Lin jl254@illinois.edu, Tian Wang Shtimwang@gmail.com, Kun Qian kunqian699@gmail.com
arxiv-2503-24289.description: Abstract We propose Rec-R1 , a general reinforcement learning framework that bridges large language models (LLMs) with recommendation systems through closed-loop optimization. Unlike prompting and supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Rec-R1 directly optimizes LLM generation using feedback from a fixed, black-box recommendation model—without relying on synthetic SFT data from proprietary models like GPT-4o.

arxiv-2510-19443.title: The impact of superradiance on the spin evolution of variably accreting massive black holes 2015 The impact of superradiance on the spin evolution of variably accreting massive black holes – B
arxiv-2510-19443.creator: Adithya Nandakumar, Ricarda S. Beckmann, Vid Iršič
arxiv-2510-19443.description: Abstract This paper explores how time-varying increases in mass accretion onto rapidly spinning black holes influence their long-term spin evolution when affected by superradiance - a process where energy is extracted from the black hole by a surrounding axion field.

arxiv-2511-07452.title: Real and complex spherical designs and their Gramian
arxiv-2511-07452.creator: Shayne Waldron
arxiv-2511-07452.description: Abstract If a (weighted) spherical design is defined as an integration (cubature) rule for a unitarily invariant space P P of polynomials (on the sphere), then any unitary image of it is also such a spherical design. It therefore follows that such spherical designs are determined by their Gramian (Gram matrix).

arxiv-2601-16920.creator: Ryan T. Smith, James A. McLaughlin, Gert J. J. Botha
arxiv-2601-16920.description: Abstract The nature of MHD waves within inhomogeneous media is fundamental to understanding and interpreting wave behavior in the solar atmosphere. We investigate fast magnetoacoustic wave behavior within gravitationally stratified, magnetically inhomogeneous media, by studying a magnetic environment containing a simple 2D X-type magnetic null point.

pmc-10594364.creator: David F Lo, Jaylyn Thompson

pmc-10702431.title: Assessing the Relative Importance of Satellite-Detected Methane Superemitters in Quantifying Total Emissions for Oil and Gas Production Areas in Algeria
pmc-10702431.creator: S Naus, J D Maasakkers, R Gautam, M Omara, R Stikker, A K Veenstra, B Nathan, I Irakulis-Loitxate, L Guanter, S Pandey, M Girard, A Lorente, T Borsdorff, I Aben
pmc-10702431.description: Methane emissions from oil and gas production provide an important contribution to global warming. We investigate 2020 emissions from the largest gas field in Algeria, Hassi R’Mel, and the oil-production-dominated area Hassi Messaoud. We use methane data from the high-resolution (20 m) Sentinel-2 instruments to identify and estimate emission time series for 11 superemitters (including 10 unlit flares).

pmc-10707894.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of 2-Substituted Quinazolin-4(3H)-Ones with Antiproliferative Activities
pmc-10707894.creator: Maria Karelou, Dionysis Kampasis, Amalia D. Kalampaliki, Leentje Persoons, Andreas Krämer, Dominique Schols, Stefan Knapp, Steven De Jonghe, Ioannis K. Kostakis
pmc-10707894.description: Sixteen new 2-substituted quinazolines were synthesized using a straightforward methodology starting from 2-methoxybezoic acid or 3-methoxy-2-naphthoic acid. The anti-proliferative activity of the target compounds was evaluated against nine cancer cell lines. Additionally, all the compounds were screened for their potency and selectivity against a panel of 109 kinases and four bromodomains, using Differential Scanning Fluorimetry (DSF).

pmc-11361341.title: A Systematic Approach to Optimize the Implementation of Precision Oncology in Clinical Practice: A Meeting Proceeding
pmc-11361341.creator: Abdul Rahman Jazieh, Nihal El Rouby, Andrew Guinigundo, Karen M. Huelsman, Emily Curran, Rafiullah Khan, Jaime Grund, Alejandro R. Calvo, Jason J. Claes, Sarah C. Overton, Sally Hellard, Leah Vasiliadis, Minetta Liu, Burns C. Blaxall
pmc-11361341.description: maximizing its use in practice. This article presents expert recommendations and best practices on how to overcome these challenges to build an effective precision oncology (PO) program. A multidisciplinary panel of experts convened to address the topic at the Precision Oncology Forum on March 11, 2023.

pmc-11546872.title: Magnetic MgFeO@BC Derived from Rice Husk as Peroxymonosulfate Activator for Sulfamethoxazole Degradation: Performance and Reaction Mechanism
pmc-11546872.creator: Tong Liu, Chen-Xuan Li, Xing Chen, Yihan Chen, Kangping Cui, Qiang Wei, Haiyang Gao
pmc-11546872.description: Heterogeneous Mg-Fe oxide/biochar (MgFeO@BC) nanocomposites were synthesized by a co-precipitation method and used as biochar-based catalysts to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) for sulfamethoxazole (SMX) removal. The optimal conditions for SMX degradation were examined as follows: pH 7.0, MgFeO@BC of 0.4 g/L, PMS concentration of 0.6 mM and SMX concentration of 10.0 mg/L at 25 ℃.

pmc-11672386.title: Cerebral infarction presenting with bilateral sudden deafness as the primary symptom: a case report
pmc-11672386.creator: Jie Zhang, Lin Zhou, Tao Liu, Yuhan Cheng, Yanling Dou
pmc-11672386.description: The current case report presents a rare occurrence of cerebral infarction with bilateral sudden deafness as the primary symptom. The patient was a 59-year-old man with hypertension who tested positive for new coronary antibodies and had a long history of smoking and alcohol consumption.

pmc-11710411.title: Evidence for a role of adaptive immunity in Tau‐mediated neurodegeneration
pmc-11710411.creator: David M Holtzman
pmc-11710411.description: BackgroundRecent evidence suggests both the innate and adaptive immune system are involved in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease. We recently showed that the number of T cells, especially cytotoxic T cells, are increased in areas of tauopathy both in an animal model of tau‐mediated neurodegeneration as well as in the AD brain.

pmc-12423338.title: Using digital escape rooms to enhance data analysis skills and student experience in a higher education human physiology module
pmc-12423338.creator: Nicola Morgan, Marriam Yaqoob, Matthew Allan Jones
pmc-12423338.description: Active and gamified teaching methods have garnered significant interest, with an increased demand for higher education institutions to enhance student engagement. One popular example of active learning is the escape room. Escape rooms are playful tools reported to increase students’ key transferable skills, which are valuable for students to boost their employability.

pmc-12631050.title: Patterns of In-patient Antibiotic Use among COVID-19 Patients in a Tertiary Government Hospital: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Survey
pmc-12631050.creator: Alshan Ruccini D. Sicat, Mark Ryan G. Langit
pmc-12631050.description: BackgroundThe occurrence of the COVID-19 pandemic resulted in increased risk of developing antimicrobial resistance due to the high utilization of antimicrobial agents. Since antimicrobial utilization is a crucial driver in the development of antimicrobial resistance, the need for antimicrobial use surveillance is crucial in identifying prescription patterns that would help provide proper interventions.

pmc-13343916.title: Joint association of atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and body roundness index (BRI) with cardiometabolic multimorbidity in adults in Guangzhou, China
pmc-13343916.creator: Haonan Li, Chunzi Zeng, Zhifeng Li, Yuting Qin, Yujie Peng, Jiahe Feng, Jie Huang, Shiyun Luo, Jun Yuan, Jing Gu, Yan Li
pmc-13343916.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is one of the most prevalent patterns of multimorbidity worldwide and presents a growing challenge to public health. Metabolic dysregulation and visceral adipose play central roles in the development of CMM. The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) has been proposed as a comprehensive indicator of lipid metabolic abnormalities, whereas the body roundness index (BRI) is a novel anthropometric measure reflecting central obesity and visceral adipose tissue (VAT).

pmc-13436001.title: Neurological complications induced by checkpoint inhibitors: characterising the clinical spectra
pmc-13436001.creator: Anne Merel van Wylick, Martin van den Bent, Bart C Jacobs, Maarten Titulaer, Jeroen Kerstens, Esther Brusse, Ron H J Mathijssen, Daphne W Dumoulin, Astrid A M van der Veldt, Marjolein Geurts
pmc-13436001.description: BackgroundTimely recognition of immune checkpoint immune-related neurological adverse events (irNAEs) is critical given their potential severity, yet remains challenging due to limited clinical experience. This study investigates clinical presentation and management of irNAEs from a neurological perspective.MethodsWe retrospectively identified all patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) at Erasmus MC Cancer Institute, Rotterdam, The Netherlands between 2017 and 2024.

pmc-13566418.title: A systematic review of qualitative research on HIV and food insecurity in high-income countries
pmc-13566418.creator: Emily Jay Nicholls, P Bicarregui, Anna Brewster, Indrajit Ghosh, Stuart Flanagan, Shema Tariq
pmc-13566418.description: Objective(s):Food insecurity leads to adverse health outcomes in people living with HIV, including obesity, poor mental health and viral non-suppression. Qualitative studies in low- and middle-income countries have described the impact of food insecurity on medication adherence. However, limited qualitative research exists on the lived experiences of food insecurity among people living with HIV in high-income countries (HICs).

pmc-13612809.title: Peri-delivery Calcium Administration and Postpartum Bleeding: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

pmc-13617338.title: VISIONARA – developing a concept for decentralized competency-based learning in primary health care and its proposed evaluation
pmc-13617338.creator: Judith Lübbert, Dorothee Schüle, Cornelia Wachter, Sonia Kurczyk, Attila Altiner, Svetla Loukanova, Rüdiger Leutgeb
pmc-13617338.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: To educate high-quality medical graduates who can contribute to a resilient, primary care-based health system, medical education must shift its focus towards decentralized and curricular competency-based medical education (CBME). However, undergraduate general practice education in Germany remains fragmented: theoretical content is delivered at universities, while practical experience is confined to clerkships in community practices, which often lack sufficient didactic infrastructure. This persistent separation of theory and practice hinders the genuine transformation towards CBME.

uslaw-usc-t46-s53712.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t46-s53712.description: United States Code, Title 46 (Shipping); Part C (Financial Assistance Programs); Chapter 537 (Loans And Guarantees); Subchapter I (General). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— The Secretary or Administrator shall monitor the financial condition and operations of the obligor on a regular basis during the term of the guarantee. The Secretary or Administrator shall document the results of the monitoring.
